key_insight: Vision-language navigation policies may explore effectively but still miss a target already in view or misjudge its distance. StopWatch identifies this goal-grounding gap as the dominant failure in the policies studied.
problem_solved: Understanding why fine-tuned vision-language models still struggle with object-goal navigation, particularly recognizing when the requested object is visible and estimating how far away it is.
method: Diagnose failures in pretrained vision-language models fine-tuned as navigation policies.
Distinguish exploration ability from goal recognition and distance estimation.
Target goal grounding as the key bottleneck; the supplied abstract is truncated before the proposed method is described.
impact: The findings suggest practitioners should evaluate target recognition and distance estimation separately from exploration. Better goal grounding could help agents act on objects they already see rather than continue searching.
visual_elements: Room scene with a visible target overlooked by a navigating agent.
Two-part diagram contrasting exploration with goal grounding.
Agent-to-target distance ruler illustrating distance estimation.
Failure-diagnosis flowchart highlighting goal grounding as the reported dominant bottleneck.
paper_title: StopWatch: Goal Grounding for Object-goal Navigation
paper_authors: Xinhao Liu, Yunsheng Tian, Yuheng Qiu, Pieter Abbeel, Xi Chen
